translations.english: The contacts of matter, O son of Kuntî, giving cold and heat, pleasure and pain, they come and go, impermanent; endure them bravely, O Bhârata.

explanations.en: Krishna draws Arjuna's attention to the nature of sensory experience: it is transient by definition — every pleasure ends, every pain ends. Because they come and go, attachment to either is misplaced. The teaching is not to suppress feeling but to endure the swings of experience without being mastered by them, which is the foundation Krishna lays before introducing the deeper metaphysics of the Self.

verses.sanskrit:
न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचि
न्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः।
अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो
न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे॥
verses.transliteration:
na jāyate mriyate vā kadāci
nnāyaṁ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ
ajo nityaḥ śāśvato'yaṁ purāṇo
na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre

translations.english: He is not born, nor doth he die; nor having been, ceaseth he any more to be; unborn, perpetual, eternal and ancient, he is not slain when the body is slaughtered.

explanations.en: One of the Gita's clearest statements about the imperishable nature of the Self (atman). The verse strips away every temporal attribute — birth, death, becoming, ending — to point to a layer of being that persists across the changes of the body. It is the metaphysical ground for Krishna's argument that Arjuna's grief over those he is about to fight is rooted in identifying with the perishable rather than the eternal.

verses.sanskrit:
कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन।
मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि॥
verses.transliteration:
karmaṇyevādhikāraste mā phaleṣu kadācana
mā karmaphalaheturbhūrmā te saṅgo'stvakarmaṇi

translations.english: Thy business is with the action only, never with its fruits; so let not the fruit of action be thy motive, nor be thou to inaction attached.

explanations.en: Among the most cited verses in the entire Bhagavad Gita. Krishna teaches the principle of nishkama karma — action performed without attachment to its results. The verse does not advocate passivity; it draws a careful line between doing one's work fully and being owned by what that work might produce. This teaching is the philosophical core of karma yoga.

verses.sanskrit:
यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत।
अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदाऽऽत्मानं सृजाम्यहम्॥
verses.transliteration:
yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānirbhavati bhārata
abhyutthānamadharmasya tadā''tmānaṁ sṛjāmyaham

translations.english: Whenever there is decay of righteousness, O Bhârata, and there is exaltation of unrighteousness, then I Myself come forth;

explanations.en: Krishna introduces the doctrine of avatara — divine descent. The verse describes a recurring cosmic pattern: when dharma erodes and adharma swells, the divine takes form to restore the balance. The verse pairs with the one that follows to frame divine intervention not as a single event but as an ongoing response woven into the structure of time.

verses.sanskrit:
परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम्।
धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय संभवामि युगे युगे॥
verses.transliteration:
paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṁ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām
dharmasaṁsthāpanārthāya saṁbhavāmi yuge yuge

translations.english: For the protection of the good, for the destruction of evil-doers, for the sake of firmly establishing righteousness, I am born from age to age.

explanations.en: The companion verse to 4.7, this names three purposes of every avatara: protecting the virtuous, dismantling forces of harm, and re-establishing dharma. The phrase yuge yuge — age after age — frames divine intervention as ongoing rather than once-for-all, an idea that anchors much of later Vaishnava theology.

verses.sanskrit:
अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते।
तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम्॥
verses.transliteration:
ananyāścintayanto māṁ ye janāḥ paryupāsate
teṣāṁ nityābhiyuktānāṁ yogakṣemaṁ vahāmyaham

translations.english: To those men who worship Me alone thinking of no other, to those ever harmonious, I bring full security.

explanations.en: This verse is widely cited in Vaishnava traditions as the central promise of bhakti yoga. The compound yoga-kshema — literally acquisition and preservation — speaks both to material sustenance and to spiritual continuity. The undivided turning of the mind toward the divine is presented here as the condition under which that promise applies.

verses.sanskrit:
मत्कर्मकृन्मत्परमो मद्भक्तः सङ्गवर्जितः।
निर्वैरः सर्वभूतेषु यः स मामेति पाण्डव॥
verses.transliteration:
matkarmakṛnmatparamo madbhaktaḥ saṅgavarjitaḥ
nirvairaḥ sarvabhūteṣu yaḥ sa māmeti pāṇḍava

translations.english: He who doeth actions for Me, whose supreme good I am, My devotee, freed from attachment without hatred of any being, he cometh unto Me, O Pândava.

explanations.en: After revealing his cosmic form in chapter 11, Krishna closes the chapter by reducing the spiritual path to five qualities: working for the divine, holding the divine as the highest aim, devotion, freedom from attachment, and the absence of hatred for any living being. The verse is often described as a summary of the entire Gita in a single sloka.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज।अहं त्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः॥
verses.transliteration: sarvadharmānparityajya māmekaṁ śaraṇaṁ vrajaahaṁ tvā sarvapāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ

translations.english: Abandoning all duties come unto Me alone for shelter; sorrow not, I will liberate thee from all sins.

explanations.en: Often called the carama sloka — the final teaching — this verse stands as Krishna's closing instruction. Its interpretation has been a major site of debate across schools: some read sarva-dharman parityajya as renouncing all dharmas in favour of pure surrender, others as letting go of the doership of dharma while still acting. Either way, the verse marks the end of Krishna's formal teaching and the pivot to Arjuna's resolve.

rāmaḥ prītisamāyukto vākyamuttaramabravīt

translations.english: Hearing the words of Hanumän rehearsed properly, Rāma, exceedingly delighted, said.

verses.sanskrit:
प्राप्तराज्यस्य रामस्य राक्षसानां वधे कृते
आजग्मुरृषयः सर्वे राघवं प्रतिनन्दितुम्

translations.english: On the Rākṣasas having been slain, all the ascetics, for the purpose of congratulating Rāghava, came to Rāma as he gained (back) his kingdom.

verses.sanskrit:
नारायणं नमस्कृत्य नरं चैव नरोत्तमम्
देवीं सरस्वतीं चैव ततो जयमुदीरयेत्
verses.transliteration:
nārāyaṇaṁ namaskṛtya naraṁ caiva narottamam
devīṁ sarasvatīṁ caiva tato jayamudīrayet

translations.english: Having saluted the Supreme Deity (Narayana) and the highest of all male beings (Nara) and also the Goddess of Learning (Sarasvati), let us cry success!

explanations.en: The Mahabharata opens with this invocatory verse, a benediction to Narayana (the divine), Nara (the ideal human), and Saraswati (goddess of speech and learning). The closing word jaya — literally 'victory' — is the original name by which the epic was known. The verse establishes the tradition of beginning any recitation of the Mahabharata with these names, a practice still followed today.

verses.sanskrit:

translations.english: Janamejaya said How did those great warriors, the Kurus, the Pandavas and the Somakas and the other illustrious kings who assembled from various countries fight?

verses.sanskrit:
